title: Reverse Nodes In K Group
description:
Take a singly linked chain and a positive group size k. Reverse the links within each complete, consecutive group of k nodes, proceeding from the head. Return the head of the resulting chain. If fewer than k nodes remain at the end, leave those nodes in their original order.

Change the actual node connections rather than merely swapping node values. Groups do not overlap, and the order of the groups themselves is preserved. For k = 1 the chain is unchanged; an empty chain also stays empty. A complete final group must be reversed, while a short final group must not.

The tricky step is looking ahead far enough to know whether a group is complete before touching its links. With a predecessor to the current group and a saved pointer to the following group, the reversal can be spliced into place without losing the rest of the chain.

Example 1:

Input: head = [1,2,3,4,5], k = 2
Output: [2,1,4,3,5]

Example 2:

Input: head = [1,2,3,4,5], k = 3
Output: [3,2,1,4,5]

Example 3:

Input: head = [5], k = 1
Output: [5]

Constraints:

  • 0 <= number of nodes <= 5,000.
  • 1 <= k <= 5,000.
  • -1,000 <= node.val <= 1,000.
